questions.q: Which tool is the right one to stop a record from saving when required business data is missing or invalid?
options: Validation rule
Roll-up summary field
Dashboard filter
Compact layout
questions.explain: A validation rule evaluates a formula and blocks the save when it returns TRUE, which is exactly the job of enforcing a business data rule.

questions.q: In Salesforce's save order, what happens immediately if a validation rule's formula evaluates to TRUE?
options: The record saves, then a workflow retries the rule
The field is cleared and the save continues
Approval entry criteria are evaluated to see if they override it
The save stops and the error message displays
questions.explain: A TRUE result on a validation rule's formula halts the save at that point and shows the rule's error message to the user.

questions.q: Why isn't a roll-up summary field really 'in' the record save order the same way a validation rule is?
options: Roll-up summary fields are deprecated
Roll-up summary fields only run once per day
It recalculates when a child record changes, not when the parent record is saved or viewed
They are evaluated before system validations
questions.explain: A roll-up summary field's value is driven by changes on child records, so it sits outside the parent's own save order entirely.

questions.q: What is the main reason a Platform App Builder favors declarative tools (validation rules, formulas, Flow, etc.) before reaching for Apex code?
options: Apex is no longer supported on the platform
Declarative tools are faster to build, easier to read later, and don't require a deployment pipeline for small changes
Declarative tools run faster at the database level in every case
Only declarative tools can be tested in a sandbox
questions.explain: The course's 'declarative first' principle is about build speed and maintainability, not raw performance or sandbox testing rules.

questions.q: Why are Lessons 14 (Validation Rules) and 15 (Formula Fields) taught back-to-back in this chapter?
options: They are unrelated and just happen to be numbered consecutively
They both require a master-detail relationship to exist first
They share the same underlying formula editor and expression syntax
Formula fields must be created before any validation rule can reference them
questions.explain: Validation rules and formula fields are both built in Salesforce's formula editor, using the same functions and syntax, which is why the course sequences them together.
